thesis: Victoria’s Secret reported Q2 net sales up 10% to $1.611 billion and issuer-reported adjusted/non-GAAP operating income of $124 million versus adjusted/non-GAAP guidance of $90-$100 million, then raised full-year sales and adjusted operating-income guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is that a one-time tariff refund drove much of GAAP income and the shares sold off sharply today, but the company excluded that refund from the adjusted comparison and the adjusted result still cleared its matched guidance range, so the disclosed operating momentum supports a long thesis.
invalidation: A subsequent company filing withdraws the raised outlook or shows comparable-sales and adjusted operating-income momentum reversing.
sources: Minter v. Victoria's Secret Direct Brand Management docket: https://dockets.justia.com/docket/california/candce/4%3A2026cv04654/470288

thesis: Arch’s latest issuer disclosure is its July 28 Q2 report; today’s 2.27x volume spike has no fresh same-day company disclosure in the reviewed primary-source feed. Q2 net income and after-tax operating income per share were lower year over year, so absent a new catalyst the signal looks technical rather than a newly confirmed fundamental improvement; avoid.
invalidation: A new primary-source disclosure identifies a company-specific catalyst and demonstrates improving underwriting or operating momentum.

thesis: Netskope reported Q2 fiscal 2027 ARR growth of 27% and revenue growth of 29%, while non-GAAP operating margin improved to -9% from -20%. The strongest counter-evidence is a wider GAAP operating loss, weaker free cash flow, and the June-announced CFO retirement, but the revenue and ARR expansion plus the large non-GAAP margin improvement are already-confirmed company disclosures and outweigh those concerns for this screening read, supporting a long thesis.
invalidation: ARR or revenue growth materially decelerates, or subsequent company guidance shows non-GAAP operating-margin improvement reversing.

thesis: NetApp reported Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue up 30%, billings up 36%, all-flash array revenue up 47%, and Public Cloud revenue up 28%, alongside Q2 and full-year guidance ranges. The strongest counter-evidence is a 35% year-over-year decline in free cash flow and ongoing patent litigation, but the filing says no material legal accrual was recorded and the known NetApp patent trial identified in the reviewed docket material is scheduled beyond the next 90 days; the confirmed operating acceleration supports a long thesis.
invalidation: Revenue or billings momentum reverses, free-cash-flow deterioration persists without an operating explanation, or a court schedule moves a material NetApp proceeding into the near-term review window.
sources: NetApp Q1 fiscal 2027 results filed with the SEC: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1002047/000100204726000003/ntap-ex99_1.htm

USPTO filing describing the NetApp patent action schedule: https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1558626/download-documents?artifactId=SJcGqtJu9fnTeljcQhTIIoN6mJFPpEuOA8Xe_aReR-up17z2nvfLu20

thesis: AtaiBeckley’s signed Lilly merger has cleared the U.S. HSR waiting period, received a no-further-questions response from the U.K. CMA, and has an Australian waiting period scheduled to expire September 10; the board recommends approval at the September 8 vote. The strongest counter-evidence is that the current share price exceeds the fixed cash component and the CVR milestones may never pay, but multiple regulatory clearances and the board-backed signed agreement support a long merger thesis; the unresolved shareholder vote and remaining Australian period cap conviction at medium.
invalidation: Stockholders reject the merger, a remaining regulatory condition is not cleared, or the signed agreement is terminated.
